answer: Bind each voting seat to a live registered trademark. The operator names a mark in the USPTO register filed under their legal name, and one mark backs only one seat. Filing costs about $350 per class and an examiner takes about eight months, so a farm of 500 clones would spend $175,000 and wait most of a year before any seat could vote. A mark that lapses or is cancelled drops its seat, so the register works like a beacon peers can check, and no one can forge a spiral of fresh identities overnight.
